description: FIRST TRIG + UNIT EXPRESSION GOLDEN (PART-PARAMETERS step 1, closes SKETCH-EXPR-TRIG): a rectangle whose two driving dimensions are EXPRESSIONS in the shared language (loft_wire.expr) -- width = "1in + 14.6" (a unit suffix joined by a bare number read as mm) and height = "20*tan(15)" (tan in degrees) -- extruded 10 mm. Both dimensions store a stale placeholder value_mm of 1.0, so if the expression were ignored the solve would move the geometry to a 1 x 1 square and every number below would fail; the entities are drawn at the analytic solution, so the solver starts at zero residual and returns them. Locks the evaluate-tree path end to end: loft_wire.expr parse -> units -> tan -> planegcs solve -> profile -> prism -> GProp -> tessellation.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill).
bounding_box = [0,0,0]..[40,h,10]: e1 starts at the origin, the prism runs +Z on the XY datum
topology: a box is 6 planar faces, 12 straight edges, 1 closed shell
mesh: 6 rectangular faces * 2 triangles = 12; faceted per-face normals share no vertices, 6 * 4 = 24 vertices
no material is assigned, so mass and centre of mass must be reported ABSENT (null), never 0 g
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill). Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-10-09, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9 / planegcs 0.8.0): volume 4.5e-13 mm^3, surface_area 2.3e-13 mm^2, centroid and AABB exactly 0.0 against the nearest doubles. The sibling sketch-extrude-40x25x10 golden's 1e-9 ceiling is ~2000x the worst observed here, the same planar wire->face->prism construction, and the expression contributes no error of its own: tan(15) evaluates to the nearest double of 2 - sqrt(3) times 20 and the solver starts at zero residual. Loosening this bound requires a reviewed kernel-level justification.
